page: Microsoft Azure D128pds_v7 is an ARM-based general purpose virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile features 128 dedicated vCPUs utilizing the 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64) and is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory. This maintains a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The server configuration does not include discrete GPU accelerators.

Storage capability on the D128pds_v7 combines Azure Premium Storage compatibility with 7559 GB of high-capacity integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The substantial direct-attached NVMe disk space provides fast temporary storage and low-latency disk I/O, reducing reliance on remote storage volumes for scratch and caching duties. The virtual machine does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Resource allocation on this host targets workloads that demand massive thread parallelism alongside large temporary storage volumes. Because the processor relies on the arm64 architecture rather than x86 extensions, binary compatibility must be aligned accordingly. The server is suited for distributed data processing, high-concurrency web services, continuous integration build farms, and database engines requiring fast local NVMe read and write operations.
